quizName: DMV Practice Test #5 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This is a regulatory sign. It is white with red and black markings. It tells drivers that U-turns are not allowed in this area.

questions.question: When riding in the rain, you should:

options.text: Ride down the center of your lane.
Ride on the right side of your lane.
Ride in tire tracks left by other cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in tire tracks left by other cars.
questions.explanation: The road is very slippery when rain first starts. Ride in the tire tracks left by other cars. This gives you the best traction.

questions.question: A motorcyclist should be sure not to:

options.text: Keep their knees against the gas tank while riding.
Keep their feet firmly on the footrests while riding.
Adjust the handlebars so their hands are above their elbows.

questions.correctAnswerText: Adjust the handlebars so their hands are above their elbows.
questions.explanation: Set the handlebars so your hands are even with or below your elbows. This position helps you steer with the right muscles. Keep your feet on the footrests and your knees against the gas tank. This helps you stay balanced when turning.

questions.question: The best way to stay out of trouble while riding a motorcycle is to:

options.text: Look well ahead of your motorcycle.
Ride at speeds faster than the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look well ahead of your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Watch the road far ahead of you. This helps you spot hazards early. You can react to dangers before they become a problem.

questions.question: Which brake is more powerful on a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides at least 70 percent of the motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: When approaching a blind intersection, you should:

options.text: Move into the portion of the lane that will bring you into another driver's field of vision at the earliest possible moment.
Stop at the stop sign or signal and then proceed normally.
Flash your lights and sound your horn to alert other drivers to your presence.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move into the portion of the lane that will bring you into another driver's field of vision at the earliest possible moment.
questions.explanation: At a blind intersection, position yourself in the lane so other drivers can see you as soon as possible.

questions.question: Oil drippings and debris often collect in ______ of a lane.
questions.explanation: Oil from cars and trucks collects in the center of a lane.

questions.question: During normal turns:

options.text: The motorcycle and rider should lean in the same direction.
The motorcycle and rider should lean in opposite directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: The motorcycle and rider should lean in the same direction.
questions.explanation: In a normal turn, the rider and motorcycle lean together at the same angle. In a slow, tight turn, the motorcycle leans while the rider stays upright to balance it.

questions.question: The normal recommended following distance should be extended if:

options.text: You believe stopping will be routine.

questions.explanation: Leave more space if your motorcycle will take longer to stop. Increase your following distance if the pavement is slippery, if you cannot see the road ahead, or if traffic is heavy.

questions.question: What does a traffic signal displaying a solid red arrow mean?

options.text: Drivers must come to a complete stop.
Drivers may proceed through the intersection with caution.
Drivers must yield to oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers must come to a complete stop.
questions.explanation: A solid red arrow means the same thing as a red light. You must stop completely and wait for a green arrow that allows your turn.

questions.question: What is Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) designed to do?

options.text: Stop wheels from locking up and skidding.
Lock the wheels while keeping control.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop wheels from locking up and skidding.
questions.explanation: Some motorcycles have an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS). ABS stops wheels from locking and skidding when you brake hard. It works when you press both front and rear brakes hard. Sensors detect if a wheel is about to lock. The system releases and re-applies brake pressure to keep maximum braking power.

questions.question: When should you flash your brake light?

options.text: To tell other riders you are near them.
To help others see your motorcycle in slow traffic.
To warn others you are slowing down or stopping where they may not expect it.

questions.correctAnswerText: To warn others you are slowing down or stopping where they may not expect it.
questions.explanation: Brake lights communicate with other drivers. Flash your brake light before making a tight, fast turn on a highway. Flash your brake light when slowing down anywhere drivers may not expect it.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. They tell you about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that the right lane is ending.

questions.question: Which material gives the best protection for motorcycle riders?
questions.explanation: Leather or sturdy synthetic materials provide the most protection for motorcycle riders.

questions.question: When should you wear reflective clothing?
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen in daylight. Wear bright or reflective clothing at all times while riding.

questions.question: What can happen if you lock your brakes?
questions.explanation: Locked brakes cause control problems. If your front brake locks, release it and re-apply it right away. If your rear brake locks on good road surface, keep it locked until you stop completely.

questions.question: How many alcoholic drinks affect your riding ability?
questions.explanation: Even one alcoholic drink can affect your ability to ride safely. Never ride after drinking any amount of alcohol.

questions.question: What can reduce collision risk?

options.text: Focusing only on your riding, not your surroundings.

questions.explanation: Bright or reflective clothing makes you more visible and reduces collision risk. Always watch other drivers and be ready for their movements.

questions.question: What is true about a DOT-approved helmet?

options.text: It severely blocks your side vision.
It allows you to see adequately to both sides.
It prevents you from turning your head.

questions.correctAnswerText: It allows you to see adequately to both sides.
questions.explanation: A DOT-approved helmet does not restrict your vision. You can see to the sides as well as you need for safe riding.

questions.question: If your front wheel locks while braking, what should you do?

options.text: Keep the wheel locked to stop faster.
Release the front brake and use only the rear brake.
Release the front brake right away and re-apply it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake right away and re-apply it.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks while braking, release the front brake pressure immediately. Then re-apply the brake with steady, gradual pressure.

questions.question: How long does a pre-ride inspection take?

options.text: It should only be done by a certified mechanic.

questions.explanation: Do a pre-ride inspection before every ride. It takes only a few minutes.

questions.question: A motorcycle's horn is ________ a car's horn.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle's horn is not as loud as a car's horn. Use your horn when needed, but do not rely on it to keep you safe.

questions.question: If you make eye contact with another driver, what does it mean?

options.text: It does not mean they will properly yield to you.
They will definitely yield to you.

questions.correctAnswerText: It does not mean they will properly yield to you.
questions.explanation: Do not assume eye contact means a driver will yield to you. A driver may look at you and still not see you.

questions.question: When riding in a group, riders should generally be in what formation?
questions.explanation: A staggered formation lets riders stay close together while keeping safe spacing. Use single file when taking curves, turning, or entering or exiting a highway.

questions.question: If your front wheel locks while stopping, what should you do?

options.text: Release the front brake and use only the rear brake.
Release the front brake immediately, then apply it firmly again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake immediately, then apply it firmly again.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks while stopping, release the front brake right away and then apply it firmly again. Use both brakes together for quick stops.
